To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation energy of thermoxidative decomposition of low-density polyethylene nanocomposites was affected by the surface treatment and specific surface area of the nanofiller used.

the activation energy of thermooxidative degradatio n of LDPE nanoc omposites is enhanced by surface treatment of the fumed silica nanofiller and is slightly increased by the same surface treatment of the boehmite alum i na nanofiller.
surface treatments of fume silica and boehmites alumina nanofillers have a strong effect on thermooxidative properties of low density polyethylene nanocomposites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of nanofillers on the thermal degradation behavior of LDPE.
the effect of nanofillers and their surface treatments on the activation energy of the LDPE thermooxidative decomposition.
the effect of surface treatment of the fillers on the activation energy of LDPE nanofillers under thermoxidative degradation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanofillered LDPEs were thermally more stable than the neat LDPE, and that the surface treatment of the inorganic nanofillers affected the thermal stability of the nanocomposites.

the nanofillered LDPE nanocomposite degradation was accelerated with respect to that of neat LDPE, but the nanofiller surface chemistry was the most important factor affecting the activation energy of thermoxidative LDPE nanocomposit degradation.

the activation energy of thermooxidative decomposition of LDPE nanofilled with FS and BA nanofillers is enhanced by increasing the specific surface area of these fillers, but decreased by their surface treatments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surface treatment of the inorganic fillers is a promising strategy to enhance the thermal stability of polyolefin nanocomposites.
surface treatments of the nanofiller can affect the thermal degradation of the nanocomposites.
surface treatments of nanofillers can affect the thermal properties of the nanocomposites, and the effect depends on both the nanofiller used and the type of surface treatment applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface treatment of nanofillers is more important for the thermooxidative stability of LDPE nanofillers than the specific surface area of the nanofiller.
the surface chemistry of nanofillers plays a crucial role in the thermal stability of the related nanocomposites.
the surface treatments of the nanofiller particles are important in the design of LDPE nanofillers to improve the thermal stability of the polymer nanocomposites.
